tools.name: newsletters_create

tools.name: newsletters_update
tools.description: Rename it, or change its description, postal address or archive. Give only what changes. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_list
tools.description: This account's newsletters with their pages and subscriber counts, and the email service they go out through. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_invite
tools.description: Email each person a request to confirm their subscription: only those who press Confirm ever get an issue. For people who asked to hear from the business. tools.name: newsletters_subscribers
tools.description: Who is on a newsletter, newest first: active (confirmed), pending (not yet confirmed), unsubscribed, bounced or complained. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_remove_subscriber
tools.description: Delete someone from a newsletter for good, with their history (for example when they ask to be forgotten). To only stop their issues, they unsubscribe themselves. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_write_issue
tools.description: A draft issue in Markdown. Look at it with newsletters_send_test, then send it with newsletters_send_issue. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_update_issue
tools.description: Change a draft's subject, body or preheader. Give only what changes. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_send_test
tools.description: Email an issue as subscribers will see it to up to 5 addresses (the owner, a colleague), with "[Test]" before the subject, through the business's own email service. Links are not counted and nothing is numbered. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_send_issue
tools.description: Send a draft to everyone who confirmed, now or at send_at, through the business's own email service. It goes out in batches, within the service's daily limit when one is set; newsletters_get_issue shows how far it got. It is checked first: one that looks like cold outreach isn't sent. Free. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_cancel_issue
tools.description: Stop a scheduled issue, or one still going out. Whatever went out already stays sent. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_get_issue
tools.description: One issue: its text, where it stands (with what holds it up, if anything), and once sent how many it reached, bounced, unsubscribed and clicked, link by link. Free.

tools.name: newsletters_list_issues
tools.description: A newsletter's issues, newest first. Free.

tools.name: account_balance
tools.description: The account balance, how much of it is credit bought (AI visibility and the phone run only on that) and how much free and bonus credit, what running calls are holding, this key's daily budget, the auto-reload state, and how much of this month's free reads and downloads is used. Free.

tools.name: account_get_call
tools.description: One call by id: its status (queued, running, succeeded, failed), cost and result. Use it to poll a background call until it finishes. Free.

tools.name: account_list_calls
tools.description: Recent calls on this account, newest first, optionally only failed or succeeded ones, or one area's. Free.

tools.name: account_refund_topup
tools.description: Refund a top-up paid in the last 24 hours that none of has been used yet: its credit, with the first top-up's bonus, leaves the balance, and the card gets the credit back with its tax. The service fee is kept. Without topup_id, the newest top-up (GET /v1/topups lists them with their ids). Free. Free

tools.name: account_set_owner_email
tools.description: When the account was made without the owner's email: send that person a link to confirm they own it. Once they confirm, the owner gets the account's warnings and approval requests, and only the owner raises limits. Nothing changes until they open the link. Free. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "newsletters" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: newsletters_connect_service, newsletters_list, newsletters_invite, newsletters_get_issue, newsletters_list_issues, account_set_owner_email, account_get_limits, account_search, account_get_brand, account_list_email_templates, account_save_team, account_data_locations · Private data: newsletters_connect_service, newsletters_remove_service, account_owner_link, account_search, account_set_brand, account_export_all, account_audit_log, account_find_person, account_export_person, account_erase_person, account_data_locations · Public sink: newsletters_connect_service, newsletters_remove_service, newsletters_create, newsletters_list, newsletters_invite, newsletters_write_issue, newsletters_send_test, newsletters_send_issue, account_set_owner_email, account_owner_link, account_get_limits, account_request_limit, account_emit_event, account_set_brand, account_list_email_templates, account_set_email_template, account_save_team, account_add_approval_rule, account_find_person, account_data_locations · Destructive: newsletters_remove_service, newsletters_remove_subscriber, account_balance, account_add_approval_rule.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: newsletters_connect_service, newsletters_list, newsletters_invite, newsletters_get_issue, newsletters_list_issues, account_set_owner_email, account_get_limits, account_search, account_get_brand, account_list_email_templates, account_save_team, account_data_locations · Private data: newsletters_connect_service, newsletters_remove_service, account_owner_link, account_search, account_set_brand, account_export_all, account_audit_log, account_find_person, account_export_person, account_erase_person, account_data_locations · Public sink: newsletters_connect_service, newsletters_remove_service, newsletters_create, newsletters_list, newsletters_invite, newsletters_write_issue, newsletters_send_test, newsletters_send_issue, account_set_owner_email, account_owner_link, account_get_limits, account_request_limit, account_emit_event, account_set_brand, account_list_email_templates, account_set_email_template, account_save_team, account_add_approval_rule, account_find_person, account_data_locations · Destructive: newsletters_remove_service, newsletters_remove_subscriber, account_balance, account_add_approval_rule

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
